plan.title: BFA in Photography
plan.notes: Academy of Art University measures progress in semester UNITS (the school's own term); all courses are 3 units and units are recorded here as credits. Source: the school's official program page (Core Classes carousel + Degree Requirements unit table + named general-education requirements), hand-transcribed 2026-10-01. Each BFA page publishes a 10-course 'Core Classes' carousel and a Degree Requirements table of Core 24 + Sophomore Portfolio 3 + Senior Portfolio 3 + Major 39 + Electives 9 + Liberal Arts 42 = 120 units. To reconcile both as printed, the portfolio-titled carousel courses are applied to the portfolio lines and the remaining 8 form Core 24 (see program-specific note). Major 39 is modeled as 13 'Major Elective' choice slots: the public pages name no specific major electives (they vary by emphasis/specialization and are chosen with an advisor). Electives 9 is 3 generic choice slots. Liberal Arts 42 is the page's named general-education requirements plus 'Liberal Arts Elective' choice slots to reach 42. The school publishes NO term-by-term map and NO course-level prerequisites on its public pages; the 8 semesters below are an editorial 15-unit/semester sequencing and all prereq lists are empty. Degree requirements: minimum grade of C- in all major coursework; minimum 2.0 GPA. Source is the school's own staging mirror (1wwwcleandev.academyart.edu), which renders the same official program-page template; the live-site equivalent page was not located in this pass. Portfolio reconciliation: the carousel shows 10 courses while the Degree Requirements table lists Core 24. PH 495 ('Senior Portfolio') is applied to the Senior Portfolio line. The page names no sophomore-portfolio course; PH 275 (Concept Project, the 200-level project course) is applied to the Sophomore Portfolio line as an editorial reading so the plan matches the school's published unit table - confirm with an advisor. After the core, students focus on commercial/editorial, fine art, or documentary courses (the Major Elective slots).
